claims.text: Spark plasma sintering enables rapid, large-scale reaction synthesis of RHEA/Cu composites.
Short SPS processing limits extensive interdiffusion between refractory phases and Cu.
Limiting interdiffusion and phase segregation during SPS maintains a stable RHEA/Cu microstructure.
The heat of mixing between refractory elements and Cu is strongly positive.
The starting material consists of composite or prealloyed powders containing segregated RHEA and Cu particles.
SPS applies high temperature and pressure with short dwell times to mixed RHEA/Cu powders.
An inert atmosphere, rapid heating, and short duration permit consolidation while suppressing long-term diffusion.
SPS produces rapid densification and a concurrent temperature rise.
The transient SPS conditions promote bonding at RHEA/Cu interfaces.
The transient SPS conditions limit the formation of undesirable intermetallic phases.
Short high-temperature exposure reduces atomic diffusion distances.
Reduced diffusion limits segregation associated with the positive heat of mixing and stabilizes the composite microstructure.
SPS produces a well-consolidated RHEA/Cu composite with minimal segregation.
SPS-processed RHEA/Cu composites have better mechanical properties than conventionally sintered composites.
SPS-processed RHEA/Cu composites have better irradiation resistance than conventionally sintered composites.
Longer high-temperature exposure during conventional sintering typically causes significant phase segregation.
Conventional sintering typically forms undesirable intermetallic compounds in RHEA/Cu composites.
SPS effectiveness can be limited by sample size and by excessive Cu or refractory content.
Optimal SPS temperature, pressure, and dwell time depend on RHEA/Cu composition and powder characteristics.
